headline: Council accepts $5,000 storm donation, sends park zoning change to Planning Commission

meeting.voteItem: Resolution 26-77, accepting a $5,000 donation for storm recovery
meeting.summary: The council voted 9–0 to accept a $5,000 donation for March 2026 storm recovery and sent a Maui Research and Technology Park District zoning change to the Maui Planning Commission. It also filed a bill tied to a stewardship group's funding.
meeting.recap: The council voted 9–0 to adopt a condolence resolution for a late community leader.[[0:31:21]] A resident said all 60 units at Lahaina Residential were destroyed in the fire.[[0:59:46]] The complex's board president said costs are about $35 million, with $10 million in insurance.[[1:05:29]] The budget director said caring for county-owned land fits a contract better than a grant.[[1:20:10]] A stewardship group officer testified against Bill 81, asking why the group was being deleted.[[1:27:48]] The council voted 9–0 to accept a $5,000 donation for recovery from the March 2026 storms.[[2:06:33]] The council adopted the amended resolution 9–0, sending a zoning bill to the Maui Planning Commission.[[2:13:52]] The council voted 9–0 to file (set aside) a bill tied to the stewardship group's funding.[[2:21:39]] It was stated that the intention is for the group to keep receiving funding.[[2:21:44]]
decided: The council accepted a $5,000 donation for recovery from the March 2026 storms.
A motion was made to approve a new county land lease for Women Helping Women at $1 rent, but no vote is heard in the recording.
The council suspended a council rule so the resolution could be adopted at the same meeting it was amended.
The council referred a resolution on extra pay for special counsel in wildfire lawsuits to the Government Relations, Ethics, and Transparency Committee.
Bill 77, on using the Affordable Housing Fund for the houseless population, was sent to a different committee than first proposed.
The council voted to file a bill tied to the stewardship group's funding.
Bill 82 passed first reading on a voice vote with no count stated.
meeting.next: The Maui Planning Commission will consider the proposed zoning bill. The chair asked the vice chair to speak with the budget director about a needed budget adjustment after the property vote.

moments.q: "Bottom line is we just want to go home."

issues.oneLine: The council sent a proposed zoning change for the Maui Research and Technology Park District to the Maui Planning Commission.
issues.why: A member said the change lowers commercial space to better meet housing needs without changing the number of homes.
issues.next: The Maui Planning Commission will consider the proposal.
issues.brief: The council adopted the amended resolution 9–0.[[#1]] Bill 77, on using the Affordable Housing Fund for the houseless population, was sent to committee.[[#2]]
